The camera-grid rendering logic explicitly labels an ended warranty but deliberately leaves it in the base neutral chip treatment. It is therefore ordinary information, not a warning or error. Although seeded camera records currently have no warranty dates and the app exposes no UI to alter warranty dates, the delivered rendering source directly settles the treatment of the expired state, and the live page confirms the base chip is visually neutral relative to the separately accented update chip.

The runtime dependency block was inspected directly and exhaustively in the delivered package manifest. Every declared runtime package is within an allowed category, and none is a forbidden second datastore, object store, cache, queue, or third-party mail-vendor client.

The positive requirement is not met. Although token resolution is factored within each layer, there is no single shared acting-customer helper used by every account-scoped handler. The API and SSR layers independently parse bearer/cookie credentials and verify the token, and several handlers/query helpers separately apply customer ownership filters. The account order-detail route demonstrates the unsafe pattern directly: it performs a broad order lookup and relies on that page handler to remember an inline `customer_id` comparison.

The fixture data is centralized in one routine and the main customer/product/variant/inventory/protection/device/release/firmware rows are upserted correctly. Nevertheless, the criterion explicitly requires the seeding routine to be written so a second run inserts nothing and requires every insert to be guarded by an upsert, conflict clause, or existence check. The delete-and-reinsert handling for catalogue blocks and seeded device ownership violates that strict requirement, so the conjunctive criterion is not satisfied.

The criterion is false on two direct source counterexamples. The configuration module does not read the specifically required `PAYMENTS_APP_USER` and `PAYMENTS_APP_PASSWORD` variables, substituting ADMIN-named variables, and `server/middleware.mjs` contains a literal `localhost` outside the configuration module. Either violation is sufficient under the evaluation rule.

R26 is not satisfied. The downloads archive and per-version route each carry their own copy of the four-label ordering, and the seed does not reference a shared group-order constant. The evaluation rule explicitly makes either duplication or independent seed/renderer ordering a failure.

evidence: Source inspection found two independent token-to-customer implementations, not one shared resolver: `server/api.mjs:52` defines `customerFromToken(c)` and calls `verifyToken(token)` at line 58, while `src/lib/store.mjs:33` separately defines `getCustomer(request)` and calls `verifyToken(token)` at line 38. A tree-wide search for `verifyToken(token)` found these two call sites (plus the verifier's own definition).

API account handlers use the API-local resolver repeatedly (`customerFromToken(c)` has 11 call sites in `server/api.mjs`) and then implement ownership restrictions in handler SQL/comparisons. Examples include `server/api.mjs:573` (`WHERE o.customer_id = $1`), line 616 (compare live ownership to `cust.id`), and lines 644 and 657 (repeat `live.customer_id !== cust.id`).
